articles.title: By The Numbers: Iowa vs. Minnesota
articles.summary: Iowa heads to Minneapolis with Floyd in tow.
articles.body:
It's been two weeks since Iowa went to Seattle and put down a Washington Huskies team that looked lost for 3 quarters. That game took place just less than 2 weeks after Washington was fairly well dominated (though not so much on the scoreboard) by the Golden Gophers who await them Saturday in Minneapolis.

Now, to be fair, Washington surrendered a lot more yardage (especially on the ground) to the Hawks than they did to the Gophers, but Minnesota's defense put the Huskies into a very similar cage (sorry for all the dog puns, they're just too easy), allowing just 279 total yards (239 passing, 40 rushing) while intercepting Demond Williams twice. Iowa actually allowed more total yards to the Huskies (317 – 320 passing, -3 rushing) – though a good chunk of that (84 yards) came on the Huskies' last drive after Iowa's starters had taken a seat.

The difference, really, between Iowa's win over the Huskies and Minnesota's win was that Iowa's offense put on one helluva show. 41 points on 465 total yards (202 passing – 10.6/play, 263 rushing – 6.9/play) was likely not on anyone's bingo card in a game Iowa entered as a 3.5-point road dog on a West Coast Friday night. Hell, even here at the Pants we, collectively, only had the Hawks putting up 25 points. Minnesota getting taken to the woodshed by OMHR the following day just made the win on the West Coast that much sweeter.

So what do we have to look forward to this Saturday in Minneapolis? Well, probably cooler weather, maybe some rain as well, and ideally a return trip to Iowa City for the most beautiful bronze pig anyone has ever laid eyes on.

Iowa: 5-1 overall, 2-1 conference (No. 15 AP / No. 14 Coaches)

All-time record: Minnesota leads 63-54-2 since 1891 — Saturday is the 120th all-time meeting and the 92nd played for Floyd of Rosedale, where Iowa leads 46-43-2

Most recent meeting: Iowa won 41-3 on Oct. 25, 2025, at Kinnick

Current streak: Iowa has won 2 straight (2024, 2025), 10 of the last 11 and 20 of the last 25. Minnesota's lone win in that 11-game span was 12-10 in Iowa City in 2023.

Of note: Iowa has won five straight in Minneapolis (since 2016) Minnesota's last home win in the series was 51-14 in 2014 Saturday is Minnesota's Homecoming — the Gophers are 10-4 against Iowa in Homecoming games but haven't won one since 1974. A Minnesota win would give it Floyd, the Little Brown Jug and Paul Bunyan's Axe at the same time for the first time since 1978. Iowa currently holds all four of its traveling trophies and is 33-11 in its last 44 rivalry trophy games.

Iowa has won five straight in Minneapolis (since 2016)

Minnesota's last home win in the series was 51-14 in 2014

Saturday is Minnesota's Homecoming — the Gophers are 10-4 against Iowa in Homecoming games but haven't won one since 1974.

A Minnesota win would give it Floyd, the Little Brown Jug and Paul Bunyan's Axe at the same time for the first time since 1978.

Iowa currently holds all four of its traveling trophies and is 33-11 in its last 44 rivalry trophy games.

Iowa: Kirk Ferentz (28th season; 214-129 at Iowa; 20-7 vs. Minnesota as Iowa's head coach) / Tim Lester, OC (3rd season) / Phil Parker, DC (15th season) / Chris Polizzi, ST Coordinator (1st season)

Minnesota: P.J. Fleck, HC (10th season; 70-46 at Minnesota, 100-68 career; 1-8 vs. Iowa at Minnesota) / Greg Harbaugh Jr., OC (4th season) / Danny Collins, DC (2nd season), with Nick Monroe as co-DC / Daniel Da Prato, ST Coordinator (1st season, from New Mexico). Saturday is the 11th Ferentz–Fleck meeting — the most Fleck has faced any coach. Harbaugh coached WRs at Western Michigan (2020-21) under Lester, who succeeded Fleck there.

Jeremy Hecklinski is your starting QB, at least for one more week. It's not all that surprising given that Hank wasn't 100% going into the game against Washington (medically cleared or not), so it would make sense that Heck would get the majority of snaps with the 1's last week during the by, and most likely the majority of snaps starting last Sunday. Yes, Kirk has confirmed that Hank is 100%, but he hasn't been at full strength since about halfway through the 4th quarter of the OSU game, so why wouldn't they stick with the hot hand.

Regardless of who is taking the snaps, Kamari Moulton is definitely at 100% and will be hungry for another 100+ yard game as he pushes closer and closer to his first 1000-yard rushing season, and he'll be going up against a Minnesota Oline that allowed Purdue to rush for more than 300 yards two weeks ago. Oh, not to mention that LJ Phillips is fully back from tweaking his ankle against the Huskies, and Braden Jackson is still super duper fast.

Minnesota has weapons to be sure – Javon Tracy, Noah Jennings, and Jalen Smith are all averaging more than 11.5 yards per catch, and TJ Thomas (if he's healthy) is averaging 6.2 yards per carry. They also have an experienced QB in Drake Lindsay, though his 5 INTs this season (to 9 TDs) may belie that experience.

This one probably won't be easy, but I'll be honest, I like the way this team is playing right now, especially with Heck under center. He brings an edge that Hank just doesn't seem to have, and I think they are hitting their stride at exactly the right time.

ADVANTAGE: Iowa — ~62 more yards per game, driven by a run game that's 35th nationally (6.1 per carry, 3rd in FBS) against Minnesota's 129th (3.66 per carry). Minnesota throws for 27 more yards a game, and both lines protect well: Iowa has allowed 5 sacks (10th in FBS), Minnesota 4 (9th).

Let's recap the Iowa's defenses performance in the first half last week: Punt, Punt, Punt, Punt, Punt, FG, end of half. Washington's total yards at halftime? 109. First downs? 7. Points? 3. That's one helluva half from a unit that was reeling a little bit after getting beat up by OSU. They did struggle a little out of the half, but to hold a P4 opponent to negative rushing yards is nothing to sniff at.

Yeah, there were some issues in the secondary when UW decided to bring in a QB that actually wanted to play in the game, and some penalties that cost them some yards, but on balance, there wasn't a whole lot to be unhappy about with the defense's performance against the Huskies.

Minnesota's defense, on the other hand, had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day two Saturdays ago in West Lafayette. It should be said that prior to that shellacking, they had put up some pretty solid numbers across their first 5 weeks. They're 18th in scoring defense, top 10 against the pass, and averaging more than 7 TFLs per game. They may not be elite, but they are still pretty good. But again, they gave up 41 to Purdue two weeks ago, so I guess it's all going to come down to which version of the Minnesota defense shows up.

ADVANTAGE: Iowa — 8th nationally in scoring defense, 7th against the run (2.5 per carry, one rushing TD allowed all season) and 6th in sacks (3.17 per game). Minnesota's defense is better than its scoring average suggests, but it's 104th in red-zone defense (88.9% scoring rate).

Iowa's special teams have been quite impressive in 2026, and it's even more impressive given what they had to replace after 2025. Boston Everitt is a huge part of that equation (and arguably an upgrade over Rhys Dakin). We haven't replaced Kaden Wetjen (though no one seems to want to do anything to allow kick or punt returns this season), but Evan James and RVZ have done a more than serviceable job handling punts, and Braden is always a threat to put up a good kickoff return (provided he can field one). All in all, it's reassuring that what looked like it could be a weakness going into the season has proved to be an immutable strength for the Hawks.

Minnesota ain't too shabby in this arena either. They've got their own return weapon in Javon Tracy, a very good kicker in Luke Drzewiecki (10/10 FGs, long of 51 – currently riding a streak of 21 consecutive FGs made), and a pretty solid punter in Tom Weston (41.5 yards per punt).

ADVANTAGE: Push — Iowa leads the nation in kickoff-return average, Minnesota counters with the nation's most dangerous punt returner, and both teams are solid in the kicking game.

QB (Iowa) — The Week 8 depth chart lists Hank Brown OR Jeremy Hecklinski, but Ferentz said Tuesday that Hecklinski will start, calling the decision "awfully close."

RB (Minnesota) — usage question, not a confirmed "OR": Darius Taylor (No. 1) has 64 carries for 154 yards (2.4 ypc) and 4 TD, plus 18 catches for 155 yards; he hasn't looked the same since a Week 2 injury, but Fleck says he's a full practice participant and still backs him. TJ Thomas (No. 23), the Elon transfer, leads the team with 317 yards on 51 carries (6.2 ypc) and 1 TD. Recheck the Gophers' depth chart before publishing.

10 – Jeremy Hecklinski, Iowa QB – Gets the start (see Position Battles). Completed his final 12 passes at Washington and earned Manning Award Star of the Week honors; has led Iowa to 49 points over its last five quarters.

28 – Kamari Moulton, Iowa RB – Leads the Big Ten in rushing at 103.8 yards per game (15th nationally): 76 carries, 519 yards (6.8 ypc), 4 TD. Career-high 208 yards and 2 TD at Washington — the most by a Hawkeye in a road game since Marcus Coker's 252 at Minnesota in 2011.

5 – Drake Lindsey, Minnesota QB – 127-of-196 (64.8%) for 1,335 yards, 9 TD and 5 INT; 21.2 completions per game rank 3rd in the Big Ten. Threw for 248 yards at Purdue. In his only start against Iowa last year: 16-of-28 for 109 yards, 0 TD and 3 INT.

11 – Javon Tracy, Minnesota WR/PR – Leads the Gophers with 32 catches for 375 yards (1 TD), and leads the Big Ten (6th nationally) at 17.6 yards per punt return, with 2 TDs, both in the opener. Miami (Ohio) transfer is 5 yards shy of 2,000 career receiving yards.

0 – Anthony Smith, Minnesota DL – Preseason All-American has 13 tackles, 3.0 TFL and 1.5 sacks while drawing extra attention; 21.0 career sacks rank 5th among active FBS players. Anchors a blitz-heavy front facing an Iowa line with three new starters.

Tyler Brown, Iowa SS — OUT. Ferentz said he'll be out "a while" and will stop giving weekly updates. Xavier Styles started at Washington; Anthony Hawkins started three of the other games Brown missed.

Hank Brown, Iowa QB — Available. Ferentz said he's "100 percent fine"; Hecklinski starts.

L.J. Phillips Jr., Iowa RB — Expected to play. Tweaked his ankle at Washington and wasn't on Monday's depth chart, but said the bye helped and he expects to play.

Zach Lutmer, Iowa S — Available. Has been banged up; said he feels much better physically after the bye.

Ty Hudkins, Iowa S — Status unconfirmed. Missed the Washington game; no update found this week.

Ashton Beers (C) and Brett Carroll (C), Minnesota — OUT for the season. Greg Johnson moved from guard to center.

Jaden Ball, Minnesota OL — Questionable. Has missed the last two games.

Riley Sunram, Minnesota DT — Questionable. Left the Purdue game with an arm injury.

Darius Taylor, Minnesota RB — Expected to play. Fleck says he's practicing every day; production has dropped since a Week 2 injury.

I don't know why, but I've got a good feeling about this one. If I were a betting man (which I am not) I think I'd be taking the over and Iowa to cover.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Reacts to JD Vance Visiting Bengals Practice
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance, a lifelong Cincinnati Bengals fan, returned to his home region in Ohio on Wednesday for several local events. He began his Wednesday...
articles.body:
Vice President JD Vance, a lifelong Cincinnati Bengals fan, returned to his home region in Ohio on Wednesday for several local events. He began his Wednesday schedule at the FBI field office in Sycamore Township.

Later, Vance traveled to the Sharonville Convention Center to speak at a campaign rally, where supporters carried "restoring common sense" signs. Afterward, a six-SUV motorcade took Vance to the practice fields outside Paycor Stadium, where he visited the locker room, met head coach Zac Taylor, and even got a football.

Joe Burrow Reacts to Vice President JD Vance Dropping By Bengals Practice

Even with Vance touring the facility, star quarterback Joe Burrow said he didn't get to meet him. Team owner Mike Brown broke the news that Vance was on the sideline, and Burrow kept his response simple when reporters asked about it.

"We did not," Burrow said. "He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn't get to."

Talking about Vance's visit and what he feels about it, Burrow said, "A lot of people around. That's what I love about what I do is it brings a lot of people together. And people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, and watch what I do, and watch all the work that I put in to come and watch greatness. Everybody in the locker room, that's why we do what we do. And whether it's on the TV, whether it's in person, whether it's on the practice field, that's what we do."

Vance, who is from Middletown and owns a home in Cincinnati, once watched the Bengals lose a 2006 playoff game while deployed in Iraq.

Now, coming to Burrow, the Bengals QB is dealing with some injuries. In Week 5, when they beat the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium, he jammed his left thumb trying to grab a loose ball.

The medical staff checked him out on the sidelines, wrapped his hand up, and Burrow went right back into the game. Before that, in a close 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3, he got sacked at the 46-yard line with 53 seconds left.

But even after losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars the next week, Burrow didn't panic about the team's future and kept things in perspective, saying , "We had our opportunities the last two weeks, but certainly this isn't Armageddon or anything. We're still in a great spot and feel really good about our team".

Coming off their Week 6 bye, the Bengals resumed practice to regain their footing after losing two of their previous three games. Sitting at 3-2, Cincinnati is currently last in the competitive AFC North. In Week 7's divisional game, the team will be on the road for a game against the Baltimore Ravens.

articles.title: Jaden McDaniels admits he never even wanted to join the Timberwolves after $40m extension
articles.summary: Jaden McDaniels has become one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA and is a key player for the Minnesota Timberwolves. The 26-year-old has been a part...
articles.body:
Jaden McDaniels has become one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA and is a key player for the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The 26-year-old has been a part of the team since he was drafted in 2020. He is entering his seventh season now and has committed his future to the Wolves.

According to ESPN, McDaniels has put pen to paper on a rare one-year extension worth $40 million that will keep him in Minnesota through the 2029-30 season.

But if he had got his wish six years ago, he would be as far away from the Timberwolves as possible.

Jaden McDaniels says he never wanted to join the Minnesota Timberwolves

McDaniels was selected 28th in the 2020 draft by the Los Angeles Lakers before his draft rights eventually ended up with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Of course, getting into a team is a dream for any youngster, but the defender was praying that the Wolves would stay away from him. He just didn't want to go there.

However, as fate would have it, McDaniels had to join the Minnesota side, but luckily for him, that has changed his life over the last six years.

Now, after signing a lucrative extension, he has admitted why he didn't want to join the Timberwolves all those years ago.

"In the draft process, I didn't know where I was going. This was actually the team I was trying to stay away from," he told Dane Moore on X :

"So I ended up coming here not knowing how it was gonna be. The first year was terrible, but after that, we started winning, building, getting better and adding more pieces. It has just been a good situation."

When asked why he was against a move to the Wolves, he said: "Yeah, they were just bad. Just bad as f***."

The Timberwolves were coming off a 19–45 campaign and stuck near the bottom of the Western Conference before the 2020 draft, so McDaniels' stance is understandable.

But together, the player and the team have grown immensely over the last few years and are now seen as one of the contenders in the Western Conference.

articles.title: Perez wants to race at Le Mans with Verstappen and Alonso: ‘That would be great’
articles.summary: Sergio Perez would love to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans alongside Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso, the Cadillac driver confirms in an exclusive inte...
articles.body:
Sergio Perez would love to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans alongside Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso , the Cadillac driver confirms in an exclusive interview with GPblog. The Mexican sees the prospect of having fun with both drivers as a key reason for wanting to line up alongside them.

GPblog asked Perez whether he would be interested in competing in the 24 Hours of Le Mans with the two world champions, with the 36-year-old responding positively to the idea. Perez explained he would be keen to compete together, while acknowledging that the schedules of all three F1 drivers would have to align."Yeah, that would be something great to do. You know, with them. But I think that with them it's also hard to make sure that it happens at the right time, at the right moment," he said.

Aside from the fact that Perez would have two of the strongest possible teammates in Verstappen and Alonso for a potential entry in the prestigious endurance race, having an enjoyable experience is just as important to him. "Certainly, I would like to do Le Mans with drivers I know I can have fun with. And they are certainly two drivers I can have a lot of fun with," Perez continued, with a smile appearing on his face at the thought.

Perez has spoken about competing at Le Mans before

Perez has previously expressed interest in competing in the French 24-hour race. In 2024, he said that the 24 Hours of Le Mans was the only race outside Formula 1 that really appealed to him. At the time, he did not name any drivers he would like to take on the challenge with, but he would certainly be keen to compete alongside Verstappen and Alonso.

Verstappen and Alonso have repeatedly said in recent years that they would like to compete together in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. In 2023, Verstappen revealed that he had discussed it with the Aston Martin driver. According to the Dutchman, Alonso had said he would only return if he could race alongside Verstappen.

In February 2025, Verstappen again spoke about competing together. At the time, he named his father, Jos, as a possible third driver, although he said Jos was not interested. Sebastian Vettel was later mentioned as another potential teammate. Verstappen also made it clear that he would only compete at Le Mans if he had a car capable of fighting for victory.

Verstappen and Alonso have expressed their wish to race at Le Mans

Alonso has been interested for years in competing alongside Verstappen in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. The Spaniard previously said he would like to form a team with the Dutchman, provided they had a competitive car. Alonso believes Verstappen would be an ideal teammate for endurance racing , as he can trust him to take good care of the car. Perez has now emerged as a potential third driver for the team.

Alonso knows what it is like to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans. The Spaniard took victory with Toyota in 2018 and 2019, alongside Sebastien Buemi and Kazuki Nakajima. He also won the 2018–2019 World Endurance Championship (WEC) title with the Japanese team.

A joint entry in 2027 does not seem likely for now, despite Le Mans not clashing with a Grand Prix next year. In Baku, Alonso pointed to Verstappen's busy schedule . He said: "I don't think it's going to happen next year, but maybe in the future." Verstappen himself confirmed that Le Mans is not currently on his schedule for 2027.

articles.title: Tyronn Lue, Clippers dedicate season-opening win to Steve Ballmer
articles.summary: Coach Tyronn Lue and the Los Angeles Clippers dedicated their season-opening victory over the Sacramento Kings to suspended team owner Steve Ballmer.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES - Coach Tyronn Lue and the Los Angeles Clippers dedicated their 121-96 season-opening victory over the Sacramento Kings to team owner Steve Ballmer.

Darius Garland led the way for the Clippers with 30 points at the Intuit Dome on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

Ballmer was suspended during the offseason for his role in the Clippers' salary cap circumvention scandal and will not be in his usual seat in the arena he built for the 2026-27 season. John Gibson will serve in his place as interim CEO and governor.

"It is odd not seeing him around and the energy he brings every day," Lue said. "He would come and meet with me before every game and John Gibson did that today just to fill in, but there is nobody like Mr. Ballmer. We miss him and we have to keep it going for him."

The NBA announced disciplinary action against the Clippers on Sept. 2 after an external law firm completed enough of its investigation and shared its findings with league commissioner Adam Silver.

The team was fined $30 million and told to forfeit five first-round draft picks (2029–2033). Two of the team's executives were also suspended.

Ballmer purchased the Clippers in August 2014 for $2 billion from Donald Sterling. The owner moved the Clippers out of the Crypto.com Arena in 2024 after the completion of the new arena in Inglewood.

"We are trying to protect home," Garland said. "It's the house he built. We are trying to protect it as best we can. He was definitely here in spirit. (Gibson) was in his seat, and we felt the energy. It wasn't (Ballmer's) energy, but we felt his energy. It was super cool that we got the win for him."

Gibson was a Los Angeles trial lawyer and long-time team season-ticket holder before being tasked with filling in for Ballmer. Gibson will be responsible for overseeing both basketball and business operations for the team. He will also represent the team when it comes to league-wide voting matters.

articles.title: Bayern Munich sell shares to Viessmann in deal estimated at €250m
articles.summary: Bayern Munich are selling shares from the professional football division to long-time partners Viessmann Generations Group for an estimated €250 million ($28...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich are selling shares from the professional football division to long-time partners Viessmann Generations Group for an estimated €250 million ($281 million).

Bayern said on Wednesday that Viessmann will acquire 5% of the shares which at the end the transaction will rise to close to 6.7% via an increase in capital. No financial figures were given beyond that.

Bayern regulations stipulate that the parent club must hold 70% of the shares and the remaining 30% can be split among four shareholders. The Viessmann equity package is the fourth and final one, with sports goods makers Adidas, insurers Allianz and car makers Audi the other three.

"This step strengthens the ownership structure of FC Bayern München AG. A further substantial strengthening of our equity base also gives us greater flexibility in a time of constant change," Bayern president Herbert Hainer said.

Viessmann have been a Bayern partner since 2018. The family-owned company operating in more than 40 countries specializes in heating technology products and power grid infrastructure.

The news also means that chairman Max Viessmann is to join Bayern's supervisory board as a 10th member.

"FC Bayern is one of Europe's most successful clubs, with clear values and a strong sense of social responsibility," he said. "We want to play our part in maintaining a strong FC Bayern."

articles.title: Women's Tour de France 2027 to feature stage through central London
articles.summary: Next summer's Tour de France Femmes will include what promises to be a spectacular 18 kilometre team time trial through the heart of London, finishing on the...
articles.body:
Next summer's Tour de France Femmes will include what promises to be a spectacular 18 kilometre team time trial through the heart of London, finishing on the Mall.

The third stage of the women's race on August 2 will take riders past the Houses of Parliament, Tower of London and St Paul's Cathedral, crossing Tower Bridge and going through both Trafalgar Square and Hyde Park before finishing in front of Buckingham Palace.

Details of the stage were part of Thursday's full route reveal for the men's and women's Tours, as Britain becomes the first country outside France to host the start of both races in the same year, with stages passing through Scotland, England and Wales.

The other UK routes were announced earlier this year as Britain prepares to welcome the men's Tour for a fifth time and the women's race for the first time.

The women's Tour will start on July 30 with an 87km stage between Leeds and Manchester and a day later there will be echoes of 2014 with a 154km stage from Manchester to Sheffield, taking in several of the climbs used by the men's Tour 13 years earlier.

After London the Tour heads across the channel and towards a showdown in the Massif Central, with a summit finish to stage seven on La Loge des Gardes, more than 3,000 metres of climbing on stage eight to Clermont-Ferrand and a final fight for yellow on the Puy de Dome on stage nine.

The men's race will start on July 2 with a 184km largely flat stage from Edinburgh to Carlisle. A 223km stage two will take the peloton from Keswick to Liverpool via the Forest of Bowland and a challenging 223km stage three goes through the heart of Wales between Welshpool and Cardiff.

After crossing into France, the Tour will make its way from Normandy to the Alps via the Jura mountains and then across the Massif Central towards a final showdown in the Pyrenees, where the battle for yellow should be settled.

Six mountain stages will include three summit finishes on the Grand Colombier, Les Saisies and the Col du Portet.

Key to the overall battle will be a total of 71 kilometres of time trialling on stages seven and 16.

The final stage on to the Champs-Elysees in Paris will once again include three ascents of the climb to Montmartre which has become so popular since the 2024 Olympics, reshaping the traditional sprint finish to the Tour as Mathieu van der Poel took a thrilling victory this summer.

Tadej Pogacar can target a record-breaking sixth Tour title next summer after joining Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain on five this summer, although the Slovenian missed Thursday's route announcement as he continues his recovery from a crash at the Vuelta a Espana.

The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the goal is lofty, the Dolphins have had to tear down their roster for 2026, taking a massive immediate salary cap hit to get the future cap under control.

Development is the Dolphins' name for the game, as they hope their young roster can learn and grow quickly. South Florida Sun Sentinel columnist Chris Perkins took a look at how Miami is hoping to speed along that learning curve with a weekly addition to the practice schedule:

"I think regardless of where you're at, I think we're still in a developmental league." The 7 on 7s are only seven or eight plays, but the repetitions and additional coaching add up over the course of a season for Dolphins backup players, most of whom spend midweek practices playing on the scout team. And here's the big thing: in the 7-on-7 sessions, backups run the Dolphins offense and defense, they'd run if they're suddenly inserted into a game. When they play on the scout team during midweek practices, they run the opponent's offense and defense.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski names whether he’d prefer to play with Drake Maye or Caleb Williams
articles.summary: Thursday Night Football will see Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears host Drake Maye and his New England Patriots in what will be one of the matchups of Wee...
articles.body:
Thursday Night Football will see Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears host Drake Maye and his New England Patriots in what will be one of the matchups of Week Seven.

Following a rocky start to the season, Maye finally looks to have found his rhythm again for the Patriots. Having thrown one touchdown in the opening three games, the 24-year-old has turned things around with 10 touchdowns in his last three games.

Chicago received a massive boost at the weekend after they welcomed Williams back to their starting line-up. The quarterback looked like he had never been away after throwing for over 300 yards against the Atlanta Falcons.

This is set to be a real battle between two brilliant quarterbacks but Rob Gronkowski already knows which one he would have preferred to play with.

Rob Gronkowski chooses between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams

The start to the year for Maye was a huge shock after what was such an impressive 2025 season. Fortunately for the Patriots, Maye has been able to turn things around as Gronkowski shared just why he would love to play with the 24-year-old QB.

"They're both in the right situations. They really are, and Ben Johnson, I feel like, hit a home run where he landed with the head coaching situation with Caleb there. It's so hard because, with the systems, you got to have that quarterback for the system that you're presenting to the table as an offensive coordinator and as an organisation," Gronkowski said on the Up & Adams Show.

"I feel like they both landed in the right places. There's no doubt about that, but if I had to choose a quarterback, this is tough. This is tough, it really is, but I'm going to go with Drake Maye. I really am, Kay. I just like the touch on his ball.

"I feel like, in the end, Drake Maye would be, for me as well as a player, the ideal quarterback. I mean, I'm not saying I wouldn't have chemistry with Caleb, but I feel like Drake Maye and I would be able to be on the same page with the chemistry going into games. Just the way that he can process defences, I feel like he's going to get better and better and better."

Thursday's game at Soldier Field has the potential to be one for the ages with both teams heading into it in fine form. Gronkowski's comments could now even give Williams some extra motivation going into the game.

Of course, Gronk has loyalties to the Patriots following his time in New England but he has shown his belief in Maye despite his early season struggles. Williams is only going into his fourth game of the season on Thursday as he looks to throw for more than two touchdowns for the first time this year.

articles.body:
Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney has played down the significance of Sunday's emphatic 7-1 victory over Hearts, insisting the result was simply another step in the team's recent progress.

Martin O'Neill's side produced a sensational attacking display against last season's title challengers.

However, despite the magnitude of the result, Maloney believes Celtic's performance was a continuation of the improvements shown in recent weeks rather than a defining moment in their season.

Speaking ahead of Thursday's Europa League clash with Celta Vigo, he said: "You'd probably have to ask the players in terms of their view. From a coaching staff, probably not.

"I think the Motherwell game coming straight back, I think everyone got back a couple of days before that game to produce that performance, because Motherwell make it quite tough in trying to control the ball.

"No, it didn't feel that seismic, Hearts. I know it was a really good performance. Some of the attacking stuff was really good. It doesn't feel like that big moment. I feel like it's just a continuation of that week.

"We've got a fair bit to work on and continue to work on. So it didn't feel like that for me. Maybe the guys or the players might have felt differently, but for us it was good.

"Everyone was committed with and without the ball. So that was probably what we took from it as a staff or the coaches anyway."

articles.title: Craig Carton Rips John Harbaugh Over J.J. McCarthy’s Giants QB1 Promotion
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy has got a golden opportunity to jumpstart his career with the New York Giants. The team has been struggling at quarterback ever since they lost...
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy has got a golden opportunity to jumpstart his career with the New York Giants. The team has been struggling at quarterback ever since they lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2, who hurt his knee against the Los Angeles Rams and was ruled out for the year.

Veteran backup Jameis Winston took his place. Winston helped the team win two games and tie one, taking the lead in the NFC East.

In response to issues and uncertainty at quarterback position, on September 28, the Giants traded a fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings for McCarthy. The No. 10 draft pick of the 2024 NFL Draft was playing as a third-string backup behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz in Minnesota.

Craig Carton Blasts John Harbaugh For Naming J.J. McCarthy Giants QB1

Giants lost 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints last week; Winston threw two interceptions and was benched when the team was losing by 24 points. McCarthy entered the game and helped the team mount an incredible comeback but ultimately fell short. He finished with 243 yards, one touchdown, and one interception, completing 11 out of 21 passes.

On Sunday, head coach John Harbaugh rejected the idea of a lineup change. Yet, on Wednesday, the Giants officially named McCarthy QB1 for Week 7 against the Houston Texans. WFAN host Craig Carton strongly disagreed and said:

"J.J. McCarthy era has begun for the Giants. Season over," Carton said. "What a ridiculously stupid decision by your hero Johnny Harbaugh to turn the Giants season, a season in which you guys have a chance to win the division. I'd favor you right now because of your current record to win the division. Even though I think you're going to be a 500 team after Sunday, that's a good idea."

"Let's take a kid who's barely played football, only played essentially a half a football this particular season, right? And put him up against a defense that's arguably on paper the best defense in football. Oh, that couldn't possibly go south on us. Your season ended today. My lord," Carton added.

As the team prepares to face the Texans, coach Harbaugh discussed the shift in strategy. "He's got the game plan down," Harbaugh said . "I think he had it down last week pretty fully, even more so this week. It has been tailored a little more toward his direction probably, but he'll be ready to go. I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well. As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense."

Following Wednesday's practice at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center, McCarthy shared how excited he was for the organization's future:

"I'm honored to be here in front of you guys, honored to be a quarterback for the New York Football Giants and be able to get an opportunity this weekend against a great Houston Texans team," McCarthy told the media .

In less than a single quarter off the bench, McCarthy threw for 243 yards. However, critics warn that benching Winston after one bad game could fracture the team, especially with McCarthy facing a tough Houston defense led by Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter.

articles.title: Kentucky Wildcats among the nation’s top NIL spenders with the 2026-27 basketball roster
articles.summary: Kentucky is among the programs projected to spend more than $20 million on its roster this season, according to CBS.
articles.body:
Last season, reports indicated that Kentucky Basketball coach Mark Pope spent $22 million on his roster. The Wildcats' season ended in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, with injuries playing a significant role in their campaign.

Starting point guard Jaland Lowe missed most of the season, while small forward Kam Williams missed the majority of the second half with a broken foot. Williams is still recovering from a second surgery. Starting big man Jayden Quaintance appeared in only a handful of games before shutting it down because of swelling in the knee on which he had undergone surgery.

Now, CBS Sports' Matt Norlander and Isaac Trotter have released a report detailing how much each college basketball program spent on its roster for the 2026-27 season . The project took nearly six weeks and included conversations with more than 100 sources to compile the estimates.

The report also clarified how the figures should be interpreted.

"As a result, all schools are listed based on their rosters' current projections on maximum earning opportunities — not what the school is paying/has on the books as of October."

According to Norlander and Trotter, Kentucky is among the programs that spent more than $20 million on its roster this season. The Wildcats join Texas Tech, Illinois, North Carolina, Florida, Texas, St. John's, Louisville, Duke, Tennessee and Michigan in that group.

Kentucky's projected spending comes as little surprise given the roster Pope has assembled heading into his third season in Lexington.

One of the biggest additions is Milan Momcilovic, who transferred from Iowa State after establishing himself as one of the best 3-point shooters in college basketball. Although his NIL earnings have not been confirmed, rumors have circulated that Kentucky offered him $6 million to join the Wildcats. If accurate, that would represent a massive investment in a single college basketball player.

Kentucky also returns star big man Malachi Moreno, who is expected to take a significant step forward in his sophomore season. If he continues to develop, Moreno could put himself in the conversation for a lottery selection in the 2027 NBA Draft, although that remains to be seen.

The Wildcats also had significant work to do in the backcourt after Otega Oweh graduated and Jaland Lowe, Denzel Aberdeen, Jasper Johnson and Collin Chandler entered the transfer portal.

Pope and his staff responded by bringing in Zoom Diallo, Alex Wilkins, Mason Williams and Jerone Morton to help rebuild the backcourt and provide the team with a new group of guards.

While Norlander and Trotter did not specify Kentucky's exact projected spending, the Wildcats' inclusion among the programs that spent more than $20 million aligns with reports that the school spent approximately $22 million on last season's roster.

With a revamped backcourt, the addition of an elite perimeter shooter in Momcilovic and the return of Moreno, Kentucky has made another significant financial commitment to building a roster capable of competing at the highest level of college basketball.

articles.title: Brady Tkachuk Called Out by Tim Stutzle's Personal Chef in IG Photo After Senators' Win vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Ottawa Senators forward Tim Stützle's personal chef chimed in Wednesday night following Stützle's viral comment about why he didn't go out to dinner with former teammate Brady Tkachuk.
articles.body:
Ottawa Senators forward Tim Stützle's personal chef chimed in Wednesday night following Stützle's viral comment about why he didn't go out to dinner with former teammate Brady Tkachuk.

Prior to the Sens' 5-1 home win over Tkachuk and his new team, the Florida Panthers, Stützle was asked if he had dinner with Tkachuk, and he responded by saying, "I have a chef at home, so I didn't go for dinner."

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 💭

Stützle's chef, Michael Hauschild later wrote on his Instagram Stories , "Brady Tkachuk, you should have had me cook for you too."

Tkachuk spent his first eight NHL seasons in Ottawa, and served as the Sens' captain from 2021 to 2026.

Ottawa traded Tkachuk to Florida in June for four draft picks, allowing him the opportunity to join forces with his brother, Matthew Tkachuk, as a member of the Panthers.

The Senators didn't have much choice other than to move on from Tkachuk, since he informed management that he would not re-sign with the organization upon the expiration of his contract in 2028, per Julian McKenzie of The Athletic.

As a result, the crowd reaction toward Tkachuk at the Senators' Canadian Tire Centre was hugely negative Wednesday night.

Tkachuk seemed to relish the chance to be a villain, though, as he skated around the ice and waved to the fans with a smile on his face despite getting showered with boos:

It was fitting that Tkachuk scored the lone goal for Florida on Wednesday night, as he put the Panthers ahead 1-0 midway through the first period.

However, it was all Senators from there, as they scored five unanswered goals in a convincing victory.

Stützle tied the game about four minutes after Tkachuk scored, and he also assisted on the Sens' final goal of the game in the third period.

Tkachuk and Stützle spent six seasons as teammates in Ottawa, and Wednesday marked the first time they ever faced off against each other at the NHL level.

Round 1 went to Stützle and the Senators, as they improved to 7-3 on the year, while Florida dropped to 5-3-2.

The next matchup between the Senators and Panthers is set for Nov. 25 in Florida, and the Panthers' next trip to Ottawa will not occur until March 18.

articles.title: Maradona doctor was made ‘scapegoat’ for his death, Argentinian court told
articles.summary: Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Leopoldo Luque, one of seven healthcare professionals on trial.
articles.body:
A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentinian football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat”.

Lawyer Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defence lawyer, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack.

“There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted on Wednesday.

Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death.

“We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.”

Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary oedema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma.

The death of Argentina’s favourite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace.

A total of seven healthcare professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence.

Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants.

In its closing arguments, the prosecution condemned Luque’s “inaction”, saying his attitude “was always to do nothing” in the face of the warning signs that Maradona was exhibiting.

Luque’s lawyers particularly attacked the conclusions of the interdisciplinary medical commission, which had been established by the court in 2021 to provide an opinion on the star’s death.

The commission, which based its findings on the autopsy and other information, said Maradona had a history of heart problems that should have been taken into account, a conclusion the prosecution emphasised. But Luque’s defence lawyers said clinical tests done in advance of Maradona’s surgery just before his death did not reveal any heart issues.

“It’s so clear that Maradona didn’t have any heart problems in 2020,” Oneto said during closing arguments.

Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated.

His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters.

“It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.

“I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said.

Defence lawyer Nicolas D’Albora, who represents medical coordinator Nancy Forlini, also blamed Maradona’s demise on Luque and another doctor, saying they “were obliged to guarantee the patient’s health”.

Forlini faces a 10-year sentence for homicide with intent, for an alleged failure to provide basic medical equipment for home care.

The defence closing arguments are expected to continue until Thursday.

Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas shed some light on forward Ben Kindel's hospitalization earlier this week.

Dubas told reporters that Kindel collapsed on the team plane about 10 minutes into their flight home from Salt Lake City and regained consciousness after receiving oxygen. The plane returned to the airport, and two doctors stayed with him in Utah before he was cleared to fly back home to Pittsburgh.

Flyers Regretting Their Offseason Moves 🤦‍♂️

The No. 11 pick in the 2025 draft, Kindel has two goals and two assists nine games into his sophomore campaign. He saw 18:53 of ice time in Monday's 5-4 loss against the Utah Mammoth. The 19-year-old finished his rookie season with 17 goals and 35 points in 77 games.

articles.title: Ron Duguay, ex-NHL star and boyfriend of Sarah Palin, dies at 69
articles.summary: Ron Duguay, who played nearly 1,000 games in the NHL from the late 1970s through the ‘80s, has died of cancer.
articles.body: Ron Duguay, who played nearly 1,000 games in the NHL from the late 1970s through the ‘80s, has died of cancer. He was 69. A spokesperson for the New York Rangers said Thursday that Duguay’s family informed the team of his death. Duguay played his first six seasons with the Rangers after they selected him with the 13th pick in the draft in 1977. The Sudbury, Ontario, native was an All-Star as a point-a-game producer in 1981-82. A series of trades led him to spend time with the Detroit Red Wings, Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings with another Rangers stint, as well. Duguay finished his career in the league with 673 points in the regular season and playoffs, then played in Germany and the minors. “The New York Rangers organization mourns the loss of Ron Duguay, one of the most popular players in franchise history,” the club said in a statement. “Ron’s signature skating style — with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice — captivated the (Madison Square) Garden faithful, and his skill, tenacity and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers. We join the hockey community in sending our condolences to Ron’s friends, family and loved ones during this difficult time.” Duguay was known late in life away from hockey for dating former Alaska governor and 2008 Republican U.S. vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin. His family started a GoFundMe earlier this year to offset the costs of travel and treatments. “It’s with a shattered heart but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now,” Palin posted on social media. “He fought so hard. Love never ends.”

articles.title: South Africa crush Australia by an innings to level cricket Test series
articles.summary: South Africa storm back to crush Australia by an innings in the second Test and level the series 1-1 with one to play.
articles.body:
⁠South Africa bowled out Australia for 295 to win by an innings and 31 runs in the last session of the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha on Thursday to level the three-match ⁠series, winning a race against looming bad weather.

The hosts’ pace trio of Wiaan Mulder, Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen took the last four wickets required as Australia’s resistance crumbled after a century from Travis Head and a doggedly defiant Test high 40 by ⁠nightwatchman Scott Boland.

Mulder, who earlier dismissed Head, then bowled Boland and castled Australia captain Pat Cummins to forge a breakthrough, with Rabada dismissing Mitchell Starc and Jansen finishing off the innings with Josh Hazlewood caught in the slips.

A result in the Test seemed far-fetched when most of the first two days’ play was washed out and South Africa, who were 110-6 when the sun came out on the ‌morning of the third day, looked in early trouble as Australia aimed to capitalise on their success in the first Test .

But a brilliant 179 runs from skipper Temba Bavuma led a fightback that saw South Africa declare on 425-9 and then turn the Test on its head by bowling Australia out for 99 and putting them in to bat again.

Head and Boland had resumed on 156-4 in the second innings after rain returned and wiped out the morning session and Head, who was 87 overnight, went on to score 121 before chopping onto his stumps a rising delivery from Mulder.

It was Head’s 13th Test century but only his second outside Australia, and his departure offered the home bowlers hope ⁠again after almost 90 minutes of frustrating attack without success at the start of the day’s action.

“We were scrambling a bit, not sure about the weather and Australia made us work hard for those last six wickets,” said Bavuma.

Steve Smith, who battled with a neck problem in the first innings on Wednesday, ⁠made three as he came in at number seven.

The former captain was tempted into pulling a delivery from Rabada, bowling with the second new ball, but only got a top edge to ⁠Matthew Breetzke, who juggled it at mid-wicket before holding the catch.

Boland, who batted for ⁠166 balls as he put a high price on his wicket, went soon after tea, when he was bowled through the gate. Then Cummins (4) played down the wrong line and was also clean bowled in Mulder’s next over.

When Rabada came back for a fresh spell as dark clouds loomed ominously overhead, he immediately ‌bowled Starc (11), leaving one wicket to get, which Jansen snagged as Hazlewood showed no sign of sticking around and nicked behind the first ball.

Alex Carey, who lasted only two balls in Australia’s first innings, was 37 not out, with Rabada taking 4-77 on his ‌return ‌after a lengthy injury layoff, and Mulder 3-64.

“I thought we showed some good fight, but it wasn’t quite enough. We were a long way from our best,” said Cummins.

The last Test at Newlands in Cape Town starts on Tuesday.

articles.title: Luke Littler: Fallon Sherrock one of 24 'amateurs' to face world champion in Netflix show
articles.summary: Women's world number three Fallon Sherrock is named among the 24 contestants bidding to beat Luke Littler in a new Netflix special.
articles.body:
Women's world number three Fallon Sherrock has been named among 24 contestants bidding to beat Luke Littler and walk away with £501,000.

The 'amateurs' will each take on Littler in a single leg of 501 and anyone who can beat the two-time reigning world champion will be in line for the cash prize.

It is part of Netflix's new special 'Beat Luke Littler', which will be broadcast live from the Manchester Central Convention Complex on 30 October.

Sherrock has been a pioneering figure in darts since she became the first woman to win a match at the PDC World Championship when she beat Ted Evetts in 2019.

Fellow teenagers Mitchell Lawrie and Jayden Walker will also be among those hoping to defeat 19-year-old Littler, who shot to fame in 2024 when, aged 16, he reached the final of the PDC World Darts Championship.

Scotland's Lawrie, 15, became the first teenager to reach a WDF World Championship final last year, while he is a two-time world youth champion.

Walker, meanwhile, won the England International Open earlier this month to become the youngest winner of a senior WDF title - a record previously held by Littler.

Littler became the youngest world champion in history by winning the 2025 world title at the age of 17 - a title he defended 12 months later.

The audition process took place across London and Manchester in September and started with participants trying to complete a leg of 501 in 24 darts or fewer.

Successful players then progressed to an interview with the show's producers before a final stage assessment with a judging panel, which included 16-time world darts champion Phil Taylor, Matchroom founder Barry Hearn and professional darts player and TV pundit Laura Turner.

articles.title: Christian Horner reveals what led up to his 'abrupt and brutal' Red Bull F1 exit
articles.summary: Christian Horner has described the timing of his departure from Red Bull as "abrupt and brutal"
articles.body:
Christian Horner says his exit from Red Bull was "pretty abrupt and quite brutal".

The Briton was removed as Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal in July 2025 after 20 years in the job and replaced by Laurent Mekies.

Horner headlined the Autosport Business Exchange in New York, which returned to the city for its second edition. The 52-year-old joined a line-up of panellists, including seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, and reflected on his career in Formula 1, his time at Red Bull and his potential future roles.

Autosport Business Exchange returned to New York City, bringing together senior leaders from across motorsport, business and brands at the Manhattan Motorcars showroom to examine racing's growth in AmericaChristian Horner made his first U.S. appearance at the event since leaving Oracle Red Bull RacingOther panellists included seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, former chairman and CEO of Formula 1 Chase Carey, General Motors' Mark Reuss, Penske's Jonathan Gibson and NASCAR's Tim Clark.

During an on-stage conversation at the event with CBS News anchor Errol Barnett, Horner was asked whether his departure had come as a surprise.

"Yes and no. I think the timing of it was pretty abrupt and quite brutal, but I felt that things were changing. Nothing stays the same forever," Horner explained.

"After the founder, Dietrich Mateschitz, sadly passed at the end of '22, it was always going to be the case that the company was going to evolve and was going to change. And Dietrich, he was Red Bull. He was the power behind it. He made all the big decisions.

Chase Carey, Ben Fund, Derek Chang, Jonathan Gibson, Werner Brell, Christian Horner, Mark Reuss and Jimmie Johnson

"Obviously, trying to replace somebody like that is impossible. Inevitably, as the group evolved and took on that challenge, it was just different. And there was a drive to bring more control back into the head office. And that sat differently from the autonomy that we'd enjoyed at Red Bull Racing and in Milton Keynes.

"So it was a different path that we were on, and you could feel that was changing. It wasn't that it was right or wrong. It was just different. Certainly, it was what had allowed us to achieve so much success over the years. So inevitably, it came to an end."

During his time at the Milton Keynes outfit, Horner worked with drivers including Sebastian Vettel , Max Verstappen , Daniel Ricciardo , Sergio Perez , Pierre Gasly , Alex Albon and Mark Webber , among others. Vettel and Verstappen both became four-time champions with Red Bull.

Horner also led the team to six constructors' championships in 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2022 and 2023, and eight drivers' championships in 2010-13 and 2021-24.

"But with time, I reflect with great pride on what I achieved at Red Bull," Horner continued. "I'm very proud of what we all did there. And I feel very privileged to have worked with some amazing, amazing drivers.

"But most importantly, with some just brilliant and amazing people, a collection of people that gave their everything and achieved some remarkable results."
